//: Each report's moment is also its first role's first test, so that the binder draws no dice outside the moment's year. THE FAMILY: BIRTHS, CHILDREN, THE SPOUSE, ILLNESS, OLD AGE AND THE WILL (docs/events/family.md). Threads: the_other_family_asks_for_the_child may mark a child fostered (and hidden), read at sixteen by the_fostered_child_comes_home; kin_left_behind may mark two of your blood stood_together, read by kin_stand_together when one fails, or mark the other slighted (the_slighted_kinsman, succession.json); a_life_of_their_own may mark a child doubted_by_the_head, read by you_were_wrong_about_them when they have what they wanted; while_you_were_ill may mark the keeper kept_the_house, read by they_ask_you_to_stand_aside, which may mark them promised_the_seat (read by the_day_you_named, whose breaking marks them defiant) or slighted. Once-a-person marks: named_a_child, heard_left_behind, spouse_ambition_heard, torn_between, heard_at_the_will. Core marks: DynastySystem born_to_the_house, schooling_begins, kin_came_of_age, grandchild_of_the_head (char); CourtshipSystem in_law (char), wedding_remembered; HouseholdSystem left_unpaid (char).

effects.text: {self.name} gave a naming feast for {child.name}, and the city heard of it.
{child.name} was named for {spouse.name}'s family.
{child.name} was named for the old line of {self.house}.
{self.name} and {spouse.name} named {child.name} with nobody else in the room.
{self.name} went to see {grandchild.name}, newly born, on the day.
{self.name} sent a gift from the house for {grandchild.name}, newly born.
{self.name} sent a blessing to {parent.name} for the child, and kept to the day's work.
{child.name} has gone to be raised in {in_law.house}, at {in_law.name}'s asking.
{self.name} kept {child.name} at home, and thanked {in_law.name} for the offer.
{in_law.name}'s tutor has come to {self.house} to teach {child.name}.
{child.name} has gone to be raised in {in_law.house}, and {self.name} had something in return for it.
{self.name} gave a feast for {child.name}, home from fostering.
{child.name}, home from fostering, is at {self.name}'s side from the first day.
{child.name} came home from fostering, and keeps both houses.
{self.name} told {child.name}, home from fostering, that this house is theirs and only this one.
{self.name} stood with {winner.name}, and {other.name} took it as a slight.
{self.name} found something from the house for {other.name}.
{self.name} told {winner.name} and {other.name} to stand together, and they have.
{self.name} left {winner.name} and {other.name} to it.
{helper.name} saw {fallen.name} through a bad time.
{self.name} went to {fallen.name} and {helper.name} together.
{self.name} spoke where it counted for {fallen.name}, before {helper.name} could.
{self.name} and {spouse.name} kept their wedding day with a feast for both families.
{self.name} and {spouse.name} kept their wedding day between the two of them.
{self.name} let the wedding day pass like any other.
On their wedding day {self.name} and {spouse.name} said aloud what had gone wrong between them.
{self.name} spoke for {spouse.name}, who is {spouse.rankName} now.
{self.name} put their own name to {spouse.name}'s promotion, and it is called favour.
{self.name} told {spouse.name} it was for their own family to speak for them.
{self.name} told {spouse.name} the house needed them more than their service did.
{self.name} let {spouse.name} write home to {spouse.house} through the war.
{self.name} stopped {spouse.name}'s letters to {spouse.house} while the war lasts.
{spouse.name} carried an offer of peace to {spouse.house}, and it was taken.
{self.name} blessed {kid.name}'s choice of service before the house.
{self.name} wrote a letter for {kid.name}, who is {kid.rankName} already.
{kid.name} is to learn the house's business for a year before the service.
{self.name} told {kid.name} it was the wrong road. {kid.name} has taken it all the same.
{self.name} told {kid.name}, in so many words, that {self.name} had been wrong about them.
{self.name} raised a cup to {kid.name}, and said nothing of the old argument.
{self.name} told {kid.name} they had been lucky.
{self.name} thanked {keeper.name} for keeping the house, and left them at the work.
{self.name} asked {keeper.name} what they would change in the house, and changed it.
{self.name} took the house's business back from {keeper.name}, and went through all of it.
{self.name} laid the house down in life to {keeper.name}, and stays on as its elder.
{self.name} promised {keeper.name} the seat, on a day to come.
{self.name} told {keeper.name} they would have the seat when {self.name} was dead, and not before.
{self.name} kept their word, and laid the house down to {keeper.name}.
{self.name} asked {keeper.name} for one more year.
{self.name} broke the promise of the seat to {keeper.name}, who will not forget it.
{self.name} gave {sibling.name} a portion from the treasury after the reading.
{self.name} kept {sibling.name} close after the reading, and asked their advice.
{self.name} spoke to {sibling.name} alone after the reading.
{self.name} told {sibling.name} that the house was one, and that it was {self.name}'s.
{self.name} paid {leaver.name} what the house owed, and more.
{self.name} went to {leaver.name} in person about the unpaid years.
It is said in the city that {leaver.name} was let go for cause.
{leaver.name} told the city how the house pays its people, and the city listened.
